Q: What is a Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN)?
Option1: A physical switch used to connect devices
Option2: A method of segmenting a network logically within the same physical switch
Option4: A device that boosts wireless signal strength

Q: What is stored in a VLAN database?
Option1: All device IP addresses
Option2: Configuration details for VLANs on a switch
Option3: MAC addresses of all connected devices

Q: What is a Switch Virtual Interface (SVI)?
Option1: A physical port on a switch
Option2: A virtual interface used for managing the switch and enabling Layer 3 communication
Option3: A protocol for encrypting VLAN traffic

Q: What is a Native VLAN?
Option1: A VLAN configured for carrying management traffic
Option2: The default VLAN for untagged traffic on a trunk port
Option3: A VLAN used for secure voice traffic
Option4: A VLAN assigned to wireless devices only

Q: What is a Voice VLAN?
Option1: A VLAN dedicated to carrying voice over IP (VoIP) traffic
Option2: A VLAN that encrypts all network data
Option3: A VLAN used only for video conferencing
Option4: A VLAN for storing audio files

Q: What is 802.1Q tagging?
Option1: A protocol for dynamically assigning IP addresses
Option2: A method for identifying VLAN membership in Ethernet frames
Option3: A system for encrypting VLAN traffic

Q: What is link aggregation?
Option1: The process of combining multiple network connections for increased throughput and redundancy
Option2: A method for encrypting trunk links
Option4: A routing protocol for aggregating networks

Q: What does network speed refer to in switch configuration?
Option1: The total amount of data the switch can store
Option2: The rate at which data is transmitted over a network connection
Option4: The time taken for spanning tree to converge

Q: What does duplex refer to in network communication?
Option1: The amount of data a switch can store
Option2: The ability for devices to send and receive data simultaneously
Option3: The encryption strength of a network

Q: What is the purpose of spanning tree in networking?
Option1: To encrypt VLAN traffic
Option2: To prevent network loops in a Layer 2 topology
Option4: To increase the number of VLANs supported

Q: What does Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) define?
Option1: The maximum number of VLANs a switch can support
Option2: The maximum size of a packet that can be transmitted without fragmentation
Option3: The maximum speed of a network connection
Option4: The largest number of devices in a VLAN

Q: What are jumbo frames?
Option1: Frames larger than the standard Ethernet size, used to improve efficiency in large data transfers
Option2: Frames that contain multiple VLAN tags
Option4: Frames used exclusively for voice traffic

Q: Which configuration allows multiple VLANs to share a single physical link between switches?
Option1: Switch Virtual Interface
Option2: Link aggregation

Q: Which VLAN type is used by default for untagged traffic on a trunk port?
Option1: Voice VLAN
Option2: Native VLAN

Q: Why might an organization use a Voice VLAN instead of mixing voice and data traffic?
Option1: To simplify IP addressing
Option2: To improve audio quality and prioritize VoIP traffic
Option4: To allow untagged traffic to pass freely

Q: Which feature combines two or more Ethernet links to act as a single logical connection?
Option1: Link aggregation
Option2: Spanning tree

Q: Why is spanning tree important when using redundant network links?
Option1: It increases VLAN capacity
Option2: It prevents network loops that can cause broadcast storms

Q: If a network is experiencing fragmentation due to large data transfers, which parameter might need adjusting?
Option1: VLAN ID
Option2: MTU size

Q: In a scenario where multiple VLANs must communicate, which component is necessary?
Option1: Switch Virtual Interface
Option2: Voice VLAN

Q: An administrator wants to connect two switches using two cables for redundancy and increased bandwidth. Which feature should be enabled?
Option1: Spanning tree
Option2: Link aggregation
